newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power eases further on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power eases further on weather.

text.p: Bulk electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. continued to soften Friday, as temperatures were expected to moderate by the middle of next week, market sources said.

Temperatures in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district are forecast to dip to only about three to five degrees below normal Monday and Tuesday. But near-normal temperatures are expected to return by Wednesday.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Monday (excluding transmission costs) gradually softened throughout this morning's trading to as low as $27.75 per megawatt hour (MWh).

Supporting prices early was news that Pennsylvania Power and Light (PP&L) reduced its 1,094 MW Susquehanna 2 nuclear unit to 75 percent power for a condenser leak. However, prices began to tumble when the company said the power reduction would likely be short-term. The unit is scheduled to shut down March 15 for a scheduled 36-day refueling outage.
Early deals were done as high as $31.00 per MWh, but most trading was reported done in the $28.00-29.00 range, down from $30.00-$31.00 on Thursday.
Firm, off-peak PJM power prices for Monday were talked at $15.00-$16.50.
Lending some support to the market was the shutdown of PP&L's 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 2 nuclear power unit for a 25-day scheduled refueling and maintenance outage.
As demand waned in the Mid-Atlantic, swing gas prices at the Philadelphia city gate also eased into the low-$4.00 per million British thermal units area.
In response to the weaker daily market, February PJM electricity prices slipped into the $29.10-$29.70 from Thursday's $29.50-$29.85 trading range.
March PJM power was quoted about 10-20 cents lower at $24.10-$24.40.
PJM prices for April and May dropped by about 20 cents to $21.70-$22.30, while June power trading range widened to $24.90-$25.30.
July/August PJM deliveries fell by about five cents to the $30.10-$30.40 area.
PJM electricity for the third and fourth quarters was mostly steady at $27.75-$28.15 and $23.80-$24.15, respectively.
